unit.why: A single narrative about R. Yitzhak of Drohobych, who cannot sleep because he stayed silent when others mocked the Besht, travels to Medzhybizh, and is greeted and forgiven by the Besht; it ends with a moral about lashon hara and a source citation.

stories.start_quote: הרב הקדוש רבינו יצחק מדראהביטש זצוקלה״ה
stories.summary_en: R. Yitzhak of Drohobych, who could always fall asleep at once unless he had sinned, finds he had stayed silent while others mocked the Besht; he travels to Medzhybizh to ask forgiveness, and the Besht, who never knew him, calls him by name to the Torah and forgives him wholeheartedly.

quotes: ואינם רוצין לקבלו עד שיעשה תשובה
tags.why: He searches out his sin and seeks atonement and forgiveness

quotes: ראה כמה הגיע תנועה של לשון הרע
tags.why: The prohibition of lashon hara, and of failing to protest, is the point
Sleeplessness serves as a heavenly sign of sin

quotes: קרא אותו מרן מורה מורינו ר׳ יצחק בן יוסף
התלוצץ על הבעש״ט נוסע דרך כזה
tags.why: The Besht knows the stranger's name and his errand
The key scene takes place in the Besht's study house

quotes: שתיכף שאמר בידך אפקיד ישן לו
tags.why: Bedtime prayer and synagogue prayer are depicted

quotes: במסיבת לצים שעשו לצנות ממרן אלהי הבעש״ט
tags.why: Mockers of the Besht; R. Yitzhak was then a non-Hasidic figure
An outsider who never knew the Besht comes to him and is reconciled

quotes: עד שבדק וחקר שהי׳ עומד במסיבת לצים
tags.why: He belatedly realizes what his sin was

quotes: ואתם אחיי תשמרו בנפשכם וחיו לאורך ימים
tags.why: Framed as moral instruction against lashon hara

missing_concepts: seeking forgiveness (mechilah) from a person wronged
sin of silence: failing to protest mockery
